description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: choose one colour and build a collage using only things in that colour.

body.heading: Pick your colour
paragraphs: Choose one colour — let us say green. Your mission is to fill a whole page with green and nothing but green.
Flip through the magazines your adult gave you. Every green thing is treasure: leaves, frogs, jumpers, apples, traffic lights.

body.heading: Cut and collect
paragraphs: Cut out your green finds, with your adult's help, and keep them in a pile. Look how many shades of green there are — dark forest green, pale mint, bright grass green.
One colour is never just one colour. Your collage will prove it.

body.heading: Build the collage
paragraphs: Arrange your pieces on the big sheet before gluing. Overlap them like scales so no white gaps peek through.
Stand back and look. From far away, your page is a field of green. From close up, it is a hundred tiny pictures.

takeaway: A collage in a single colour shows how many shades that colour can have.
materials: Old magazines or catalogues (an adult provides)
safetyNotes: An adult should do or closely help with all cutting. Only use magazines an adult gives you for cutting up.
screenFreeExtension: Make a rainbow of collages across a week — one colour each day.
